d.d: Alternative form of eaves (“the underside of a roof that extends beyond the external walls of a building”)
The underside of a roof that extends beyond the external walls of a building.
Something that extends over or projects beyond.
To hear (intentionally) a conversation one is not intended to hear; to listen in.
d.x: I hope nobody was eavesdropping on our conversation last night, since it got so personal.

d.d: To listen for another organism's calls, so as to exploit them.
The dripping of rain from the eaves of a house.
The space around a house on which such water drips.
A concealed aperture through which an occupant of a building can surreptitiously listen to people talking at an entrance to the building.
simple past and past participle of eavesdrop
Listening secretly to the private conversations of others.
The act of one organism listening for another's calls, so as to exploit them.
present participle and gerund of eavesdrop
